item.title: Future Perspective: Digital Sovereignty and Human Dignity
item.lead: The conclusion of the dossier shifts the question from "what does the platform do?" to "what limits do we want to set for the digitalization of human dignity?"

blocks.text: In this context, digital sovereignty does not mean rejecting technology. It means that users and creators do not become entirely dependent on systems whose logic they cannot comprehend. Transparency, data portability, account autonomy, and intelligible rules form the institutional foundation for this.

Human dignity is given its own place in the dossier. The author distinguishes between a person as a consumer and a person as a human being. When attention, vulnerability, and emotional support are exclusively treated as economic inputs, there is a risk that the human being is reduced to a profile, segment, or revenue opportunity.

The future question is therefore which forms of digitalization we do consider desirable. Technology can expand reach, bridge language barriers, connect communities, and assist people. The problem arises when the same instruments are used to optimize dependency, hidden profiling, or deception.

Ultimately, the dossier advocates for a revaluation of unpaid human presence. As a policy idea, this is more than a slogan: it means investing in physical social space, creator rights, transparent digital services, and institutional control over systems that organize intimacy at scale.
